content:
ryan: quick thread — noticed ~8-12% throughput drop on short-seq workloads when FlashAttention + paged-KV are both enabled. traces show many tiny batches (1-3 tokens) piling up; queue time dominates.

maria: repro on staging or prod?

ryan: staging (eu-west). started after the kernel-selector change that now prefers Flash for median seq ~40.

devin: attaching a quick perf dump: 
```
kernel_select: FlashAttention 62%
kernel_select: ref_kernel 38%
avg_batch_size: 2.1 tokens
queue_latency_ms_p50: 18
queue_latency_ms_p95: 120
cpu_spin_ms: 6
```

sam: that avg_batch_size screams queue-slicer mis-slicing. our queue policy chops based on token_budget_target=512 which explodes small-seq requests into many micro-batches.

devin: agreed. selector picks Flash because seq_len estimate ~40, but Flash has higher per-call setup when batches are dominated by short requests. paged-KV adds async memcpy and increases tail latency for tiny batches.

alisa: proposal: lower token_budget_target to 256 for chat-like paths, and add hard fallback: if expected_batch_tokens < 96 prefer ref_kernel. quick config sketch: 
```
queue:
  token_budget_target: 256
  queue_slicing_ms: 6
kernel_selector:
  fallback_seq_tokens: 96
```

perf-bot: trace uploaded: https://perf/redwood/traces/1777777777-abc — p95 regression linked.

maria: I'll run an A/B on staging with these params. will also run a short-run loadgen that emphasizes chat-like 8-50 token responses and capture p50/p95 throughput and kernel_switch_ms.

sam: also capture batch_token_distribution and kernel_invocation_count per minute. if queue_slicer is over-chopping we should see a spike at batch_size=1.

ryan: agreed. please tag me on results. if this fixes >5% throughput we push as hotfix to dedicated pools and add selector unit test for short-seq heuristics. :thumbsup:
